security_audit.summary: The static command and reconnaissance detections are false positives caused by Markdown fences, JSX template literals, and ordinary application identifiers. One semantic issue remains because the Zustand reference recommends persisting an auth token in browser storage, which can expose credentials during XSS.

remediation.issue: Auth token persistence in browser storage
remediation.suggestion: Replace the token persistence example with non-secret session state, or warn users not to store credentials in Zustand persist storage.

semantic_findings.title: Auth Token Stored in Browser State
semantic_findings.description: The Zustand reference demonstrates persisting an auth token to sessionStorage. Browser storage is exposed to XSS and should not be recommended for credentials.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The sample explicitly defines an AuthStore token and persists that token through sessionStorage. It is documentation rather than active exfiltration, so the finding is medium severity.

content.value_statement: React apps often mix server, client, form, and URL state without clear ownership. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical TanStack Query, Zustand, and form patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use TanStack Query, Zustand, React Hook Form with Zod, and URL state.
Provides query key factory patterns for typed server state access.
Shows mutation hooks with cache invalidation after create and update actions.
Demonstrates typed Zustand stores, selectors, persistence, and computed selectors.
Includes form validation patterns using React Hook Form and Zod schemas.
limitations: Examples are TypeScript snippets that must be adapted to each project.
The skill does not include package installation commands or version compatibility checks.
It does not cover Redux, Jotai, MobX, or server cache infrastructure.
Auth persistence examples need review before handling real credentials.

use_cases.title: Plan React State Ownership
use_cases.description: Separate server data, client preferences, forms, and URL parameters before implementation.
use_cases.target_user: Frontend engineers starting a new React feature

use_cases.title: Standardize Query Hooks
use_cases.description: Create consistent query keys, enabled checks, and invalidation behavior across resources.
use_cases.target_user: Technical leads maintaining React data access patterns

use_cases.title: Improve Store Performance
use_cases.description: Use typed Zustand stores and selectors to reduce unnecessary rerenders.

prompt_templates.title: Choose State Owners
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React feature and assign each state value to TanStack Query, Zustand, React Hook Form, URL search params, or local component state. Explain the reason for each choice.

prompt_templates.title: Create Query Hooks
prompt_templates.prompt: Design TanStack Query hooks for this resource. Include query key naming, enabled conditions, cache invalidation, and loading behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Store
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this Zustand store to use typed slices, selectors, and persisted settings where appropriate. Avoid storing secrets in browser storage.

prompt_templates.title: Design End-to-End State Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a state management plan for this multi-page React workflow. Cover server data, optimistic mutations, form validation, URL state, and rerender prevention.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for a state ownership plan for a React user dashboard.
output: Server user data belongs in TanStack Query with stable query keys.
Sidebar and theme state belong in a small Zustand store with selectors.
User edit fields belong in React Hook Form with Zod validation.

output_examples.input: A team wants to reduce rerenders in a large Zustand store.
output: Move broad store reads into narrow selectors.
Keep derived values in named selector functions.
Subscribe components only to values they render.

output_examples.input: A maintainer wants safer mutation behavior after user updates.
output: Invalidate the changed detail query after the update succeeds.
Invalidate the user list so aggregate views refresh.
Use rollback handling when applying optimistic changes.

best_practices: Keep server data in TanStack Query and reserve Zustand for client-owned UI state.
Use stable query key factories so cache invalidation stays predictable.
Use selectors for Zustand reads to avoid broad component rerenders.
anti_patterns: Do not mirror server data into a global client store without a clear reason.
Do not read an entire Zustand store when a component needs one value.
Do not persist auth tokens or other secrets in browser state storage.

faq.question: Does this skill replace state management documentation?
faq.answer: No. It provides practical patterns that should be checked against current library documentation.

faq.question: Which tools does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on TanStack Query, Zustand, React Hook Form, Zod, and URL state patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with Next.js applications?
faq.answer: Yes. The patterns fit React and Next.js projects that separate server, client, form, and URL state.

faq.question: Does it generate complete application code?
faq.answer: No. It gives reusable snippets and design guidance that need project-specific integration.

faq.question: Is it safe for authentication state?
faq.answer: Use caution. Do not persist real tokens or secrets in browser storage without a security review.

faq.question: Can teams use it for code reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide reviews of query keys, invalidation, selectors, and form validation boundaries.
